niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a psychology-based approach, a specific spiritual tradition, or a mix. These are good starting points from the options I found:

### For Jungian shadow work
- **Jung Platform — *Encounters with the Shadow***: A beginner-friendly introduction led by Jungian analyst and author James Hollis. A strong pick if you want depth psychology rather than a generic self-help course. [Course page](https://jungplatform.com/store/encounters-with-the-shadow/partner/jrose)
- **Jung Platform — shadow-work courses**: Offers courses with depth psychologists including James Hollis, Craig Chalquist, and Ken James, with different perspectives on personal and collective shadow. [Browse courses](https://jungplatform.com/shadow-work)
- **The Shift Network — *Jungian Shadow Work & the Alchemy of Fairy Tales***: A more specialized option, taught by depth psychologist and author Melissa Kim Corter; best if myths and fairy tales appeal to you. [Course page](https://theshiftnetwork.com/course/01MCorter01_25?f=1)

### For a regular spiritual practice
- **WCCM — online meditation courses**: A good choice if you’re interested in Christian contemplative practice and want structured guidance for establishing a meditation habit. [Browse courses](https://wccm.org/courses/)
- **Shalem Institute — *Closer Than Breath***: A self-paced, six-week course in Centering Prayer, with an interfaith orientation. The listing I found gives a price of $75, but check the page for current availability and cost. [Course details](https://shalem.org/programs/offerings-by-shalem-graduates/)
- **Mindworks — mindfulness or Buddhist meditation courses**: A secular-friendly option for mindfulness, or a more explicitly Buddhist path. Its Buddhist courses are described as 14-day modules with guided meditations and lessons. [Mindfulness courses](https://mindworks.org/meditation-courses/mindfulness-courses/) · [Buddhist courses](https://mindworks.org/meditation-courses/buddhist-courses/)

**My short recommendation:** Start with *Encounters with the Shadow* for Jungian self-inquiry, then pair it with a gentle, consistent meditation course such as WCCM or Mindworks. Before enrolling, check the current syllabus, instructor background, price, and whether the course offers live support or is entirely self-paced.

Shadow work can bring up painful memories or intense emotions. A course can support reflection, but it isn’t a substitute for therapy; consider working with a qualified mental-health professional if you’re dealing with trauma or feeling overwhelmed.
